overview: Rapid review with documented shortcuts, updating the 2023 meta-analysis for patient-reported function at about three months and summarising adherence, physiotherapist time, patient experience and results for older and digitally excluded patients, reported to the procurement committee on 10 December 2026.
population: Adults after primary total knee replacement in randomised trials (effectiveness) and in qualitative or observational studies (adherence, workload, experience) published from January 2015 in English.
exposure: Wearable-based activity feedback in the first 12 weeks after surgery: a worn device that records activity with feedback to the patient through targets, app messages or physiotherapist messages. Comparator: usual rehabilitation or the same device without feedback.
procedures: The information specialist searches three bibliographic databases and two trial registries from January 2022 to October 2026 with a dated strategy and checks the reference list of the 2023 meta-analysis. One physiotherapist screens titles and abstracts and the second checks a random 20 percent; full texts are screened by one reviewer and disagreements discussed. One reviewer extracts data into a tested form and the second checks every primary outcome value. Trials are judged with a short domain-based risk of bias tool; qualitative studies are summarised thematically. Function is pooled if at least five trials report it; otherwise effect directions are tabulated.

outcomes.name: Patient-reported knee function at about three months
outcomes.measure: Standardised mean difference between feedback and comparator in validated knee function scores
outcomes.why: The outcome that matters to patients and to the committee; step counts may not translate into function.

outcomes.name: Daily step count
outcomes.measure: Mean difference in device-measured steps per day
outcomes.why: The behaviour the feedback targets directly.

outcomes.name: Device wear and synchronisation
outcomes.measure: Proportion of participants wearing the device on at least five days a week at 6 and 12 weeks
outcomes.why: Low adherence limits benefit and raises the cost per active user.

outcomes.name: Physiotherapist time
outcomes.measure: Minutes per patient per week spent reviewing data and messaging
outcomes.why: Clinic time is the main hidden cost of the lease.

outcomes.name: Falls and readmissions
outcomes.measure: Participants with a fall or readmission as reported by trials
outcomes.why: More walking in the early weeks could bring more falls.

feasibility: Fits 20 information specialist hours and two physiotherapists at one day a week for eight weeks if about 1,500 records are screened; protocol sign-off by 5 October 2026 keeps the 10 December deadline.
biasMitigation: Search strategy dated and reported in full
Second reviewer checks 20 percent of screening decisions and every primary outcome extraction
Every shortcut stated in the report
Supplier-funded studies flagged and removed in a sensitivity analysis

biasFlags.label: Single-reviewer screening
biasFlags.note: May miss eligible studies; the 20 percent check estimates how many.

biasFlags.label: English-language restriction
biasFlags.note: Rapid reviews more often miss non-English studies.

biasFlags.label: Industry funding
biasFlags.note: Device makers fund several trials; analysed separately.

flags: Two process and balancing outcomes reported descriptively
parsimony.simplestPath: Update one meta-analysis for one primary outcome and summarise adherence, workload and experience narratively.

theoreticalFramework: None; the question is effectiveness and adherence, and no framework earns its place in an eight-week review.
summary: Rapid review protocol with one primary outcome, one secondary, one process and two balancing outcomes, and every shortcut stated.
